contract_answer.question: Can the fade-rate RMSE gain be kept without hurting short-life calibration using an identity-preserving relative-fade residual g_t = h_t + 1[t>0] F([d_t, r_t]) with zero-initialised F output, achieving KEEP under program.md §7 vs active parent ZN-E005 (e.g. Path B RMSE <= 424.0 with MAPE <= 0.3246 and Acc@15 >= 0.3755)?
contract_answer.conclusion: Reviewed by CODEX(gemini-4-argon). Apply the proposal's primary rule exactly. On split 2021 (seed 2021, Kaggle Tesla T4), ZN-E012 is a complete, finite 14-epoch run (644 optimizer steps, 157.942s training compute, 98,113 parameters, early stopping at epoch 14 with both minimum-MAPE and epsilon-Pareto selected checkpoint at epoch 9) achieving MAPE 0.333255, Acc@15 0.3225, RMSE 423.435 cycles, MAE 229.072 cycles, and DB-MAPE 0.333255 versus matched reference ZN-E011 (MAPE 0.332726, Acc@15 0.3045, RMSE 415.830 cycles, MAE 223.475 cycles, DB-MAPE 0.332726, 102,209 parameters) and active parent ZN-E005 (MAPE 0.321573, Acc@15 0.4055, RMSE 445.047 cycles, MAE 234.104 cycles, DB-MAPE 0.321573, 85,697 parameters). Against active parent ZN-E005, ZN-E012 clears Path B's primary RMSE threshold by 0.565 cycles (423.435 <= 424.0, -21.612 cycles vs ZN-E005, though +7.605 cycles vs ZN-E011), and recovers +0.0180 Acc@15 over ZN-E011 (0.3225 vs 0.3045; <500 MAPE improves from 0.2156 to 0.2093 and <500 Acc@15 from 0.4060 to 0.4300), but fails Path B's accompanying MAPE guard (0.333255 > 0.3246, +0.011682 vs ZN-E005), Acc@15 guard (0.3225 < 0.3755, -0.0830 vs ZN-E005), DB-MAPE guard (0.333255 > 0.3316), and 20-cell ZN-coin domain Acc@15 guardrail (-0.0830 > 0.05 regression). Path A (MAPE <= 0.3136) and Path C (Acc@15 >= 0.4255) also fail. The gradient gate PASSES cleanly (overall_gradient_health HEALTHY, all 6 blocks OK in tools/layer_report.py with late near-zero fractions 0.0000 in cycle_stem, 0.0236 in residual_blocks.0, 0.0386 in residual_blocks.1, 0.0000 in fade_encoder, 0.0000 in inter_summary, and 0.0000 in head) and prediction spread PASSES (prediction SD 135.84 cycles = 33.34% of target SD 407.45 >= 10%, correlation 0.4302, 0 extreme negative predictions). Therefore the primary rule requires Decision: DISCARD. With user agreement to early Phase-1 closure (A5-ZN, diagnostics/phase1_breakthrough_diagnosis.md), Phase-1 architecture search stops here and transitions to three-seed confirmation of the best gradient-healthy Phase-1 candidate before freezing for Phase 2.

main_symptom: Gating the fade residual by 1[t>0], feeding pure relative inputs [d_t, r_t], and zero-initializing the final fade_encoder Linear layer in ZN-E012 partially restores short-life (<500 cycles, 15 cells) calibration compared with matched reference ZN-E011—improving <500 MAPE from 0.2156 to 0.2093 and <500 Acc@15 from 0.4060 to 0.4300 (recovering Acc@15 0.62 -> 1.00 on ZN-coin_402-1 [EOL 104], 0.00 -> 0.17 on ZN-coin_445-3 [EOL 183], and reducing ZN-coin_429-1 [EOL 137] MAPE from 0.477 to 0.424)—while keeping overall RMSE <= 424.0 at 423.44 cycles (-21.61 vs ZN-E005) and passing the gradient gate across all 6 blocks (0.00% late near-zero gradients in fade_encoder, cycle_stem, inter_summary, and head). However, overall MAPE remains at the structural Phase-1 plateau of 0.3333 (+0.0005 vs ZN-E011, +0.0117 vs ZN-E005) and Acc@15 reaches only 0.3225 (-0.0830 vs ZN-E005) because (1) even with g_1 = h_1 exact, the GELU-backed ResConv + fade trajectory pushes Cycle-1 and prefix predictions upward by +20-45 cycles on several short-life cells relative to ReLU-clipped ZN-E005 (<500 MAPE 0.2093 vs 0.1856 in ZN-E005), and (2) removing raw h_t from fade_encoder weakens state-dependent rate scaling on medium/long-life cells, giving back 30.85 cycles of 500-1000 bias (-424.60 -> -455.45) and 13.70 cycles of >1000 bias (-977.61 -> -991.31; correlation 0.4562 -> 0.4302, prediction SD 142.27 -> 135.84 cycles).

contradicting_evidence: Relative to matched reference ZN-E011, ZN-E012 improves overall Acc@15 by +0.0180 (0.3045 -> 0.3225), <500 Acc@15 by +0.0240 (0.4060 -> 0.4300), and <500 MAPE by -0.0063 (0.2156 -> 0.2093), while still clearing Path B's primary RMSE threshold against ZN-E005 (423.44 <= 424.0 cycles, and reaching 415.69 at epoch 11 and 414.88 at epoch 14).

At step 1, fade_encoder output activation is identically zero (mean 0.0, std 0.0, zero_fraction 1.0) as designed, and by step 185 it wakes up cleanly to late near-zero gradient fraction 0.0000, update ratio 0.00369, and activation L2 norm 3.525.
causes.interpretation: Comparing ZN-E012 directly against matched reference ZN-E011 tests whether ZN-E011's short-life calibration loss came from fade_encoder rewriting raw h_t at Cycle 1. Enforcing g_t = h_t + 1[t>0] F([d_t, r_t]) with zero-initialized output Linear(64->64) works in the predicted direction on short-life cells vs ZN-E011: Cycle-1 predictions drop closer to targets on ZN-coin_402-1 (EOL 104: p1 116.8 -> 109.3, Acc@15 0.62 -> 1.00), ZN-coin_429-1 (EOL 137: p1 202.0 -> 190.4, MAPE 0.477 -> 0.424), and ZN-coin_445-3 (EOL 183: mean pred 251.7 -> 234.7, Acc@15 0.00 -> 0.17), lifting <500 Acc@15 from 0.4060 to 0.4300 and prefix 51-75 Acc@15 from 0.410 to 0.444. However, two findings refute the hypothesis that this change suffices for a §7 KEEP vs ZN-E005: (1) Even when F contributes zero at Cycle 1 (g_1 = h_1), Cycle-1 predictions in ZN-E012 remain +25-45 cycles higher than ZN-E005 on several short-life cells (e.g., ZN-coin_429-1 p1=190.4 vs 145.5 in ZN-E005; ZN-coin_445-2 p1=207.0 vs 165.8; ZN-coin_445-3 p1=206.9 vs 165.5) because training the GELU ResConv backbone and readout jointly with long-prefix fade residuals shifts the shared h_1 projection itself, leaving <500 MAPE at 0.2093 vs 0.1856 in ZN-E005. (2) Removing raw h_t from F([d_t, r_t]) prevents F from conditioning fade rate on baseline curve shape, reducing medium-life predictions on ZN-coin_432-3 (EOL 923: mean 603.7 -> 566.2) and ZN-coin_433-3 (EOL 770: mean 240.1 -> 215.9), so 500-1000 bias slips from -424.60 to -455.45 cycles and >1000 bias from -977.61 to -991.31 cycles, offsetting the <500 MAPE improvement (overall MAPE 0.3327 -> 0.3333).
missing_evidence: No further Family-4 architecture follow-ups are needed because the user approved early Phase-1 closure (A5-ZN, diagnostics/phase1_breakthrough_diagnosis.md) to address the shared Relative Huber 1/y tail bias in Phase 2.

contradicting_evidence: Across Family 4 (ZN-E010, ZN-E011, ZN-E012), explicit Cycle-1 anchored fade and rate features consistently reduce split-2021 RMSE by 20-29 cycles vs ZN-E005 (445.05 -> 425.01 / 415.83 / 423.44 cycles) and raise prediction-target correlation from 0.2756 to 0.4302-0.4785 while keeping 0 extreme negative predictions (vs 19 in ZN-E005).
causes.interpretation: As documented in diagnostics/phase1_breakthrough_diagnosis.md (user agreement A5-ZN), ZN-E012 confirms that all nine Phase-1 architectures across four model families are pinned to a split-2021 validation MAPE floor of 0.3216-0.3635 (8 of 9 within 0.3216-0.3369; ZN-E010 0.3325, ZN-E011 0.3327, ZN-E012 0.3333) with a 0.905 mean pairwise per-cell MAPE correlation. Under locked Relative Huber (delta = 0.15), linear-regime gradients scale as dL/dy_hat = +/- delta / y, weighting the 15 short-life cells (mean EOL 191.9, 75% of samples) 6.4x-11.9x more heavily per sample than the 3 high-life cells (mean EOL 1235.3, 15% of samples). Consequently, in ZN-E012 the 3 cells with EOL > 1000 still suffer -991.31 cycles of bias (MAPE 0.8065, Acc@15 0.0, 85.41% of total MSE) and the 2 cells with EOL 500-1000 suffer -455.45 cycles of bias (MAPE 0.5531, Acc@15 0.0, 12.76% of total MSE; combined >=500 cells account for 98.16% of MSE and 0.1763 of the 0.3333 total MAPE). Rebalancing this tail underprediction requires Phase-2 loss terms (e.g., stat_tail_balance, rarity/cell-balanced weighting, and label-free physics constraints).
missing_evidence: Three-split confirmation of the chosen Phase-1 architecture to freeze the model and unlock Phase-2 loss experiments.

contradicting_evidence: Passing the gradient gate across all 6 blocks (0.00% late near-zero gradients in cycle_stem, fade_encoder, inter_summary, and head) does not by itself overcome the Relative Huber 1/y MAPE floor on split 2021.
causes.interpretation: Every GELU-backed Family-4 run (ZN-E010, ZN-E011, ZN-E012) passes the gradient gate with overall_gradient_health HEALTHY and all 6 blocks OK in tools/layer_report.py: in ZN-E012, late near-zero gradient fractions are 0.0000 in cycle_stem, 0.0236 in residual_blocks.0, 0.0386 in residual_blocks.1, 0.0000 in fade_encoder (after the expected 0.6649 step-1 zero-init transient on the second Linear layer), 0.0000 in inter_summary, and 0.0000 in head, with branch imbalance 69.58x (< 1000x) and exact padding invariance (0.0). next_action.summary: ZN-E012 is VALID + DISCARD under the proposal's primary rule against active parent ZN-E005: although it clears Path B's primary RMSE threshold (423.44 <= 424.0 cycles, -21.61 vs ZN-E005) and improves Acc@15 over matched reference ZN-E011 (0.3225 vs 0.3045; <500 MAPE 0.2093 vs 0.2156, <500 Acc@15 0.4300 vs 0.4060) with a HEALTHY gradient gate across all 6 blocks, it fails Path B's MAPE guard (0.3333 > 0.3246), Acc@15 guard (0.3225 < 0.3755), and DB-MAPE guard (0.3333 > 0.3316). With user agreement to early Phase-1 closure (A5-ZN, diagnostics/phase1_breakthrough_diagnosis.md), we must select the best Phase-1 candidate under program.md §7 for three-split confirmation before freezing for Phase 2. Why ZN-E005 cannot be frozen as-is: ZN-E005 (ResConv-MaskedSummary-H0 with ReLU) already ran its confirmation on splits 42 (ZN-E006) and 2024 (ZN-E007) and was formally DISCARD / NOT CONFIRMED on both because its bare ReLU readout failed the gradient gate (inter_summary/head late near-zero fractions 0.546/0.508 on split 42 and 0.568/0.523 on split 2024), and it produced 19 extreme negative predictions (down to -408.5 cycles) with low correlation (0.276) on split 2021. Candidate selection for confirmation: Confirm ZN-E010 (AnchoredFade-ResConv-GELU, variant='anchored_fade_resconv_masked_summary', d_model=64, residual_layers=2, d_ff=64, mlp_layers=0, summary_mode='mean_last_delta', dropout=0.1, activation='gelu', fade_hidden=64, fade_input='anchor', 98,113 params) on the remaining two paper splits BL_SPLIT=42 (ZN-E013) and BL_SPLIT=2024 (ZN-E014) with training seed=2021 (completing the 3-split aggregate across splits 2021 [already run in ZN-E010], 42, and 2024 per state.json.split_protocol). Why ZN-E010 is the best gradient-healthy Phase-1 candidate by program.md §7: (1) Among all gradient-healthy (GELU) runs (ZN-E003, ZN-E009, ZN-E010, ZN-E011, ZN-E012), ZN-E010 has the best primary MAPE and DB-MAPE (0.3325 vs 0.3327 [E011], 0.3333 [E012], 0.3369 [E009], 0.3635 [E003]), the highest Acc@15 by a wide margin (0.3665 vs 0.3305 [E009], 0.3225 [E012], 0.3045 [E011], 0.2030 [E003]), the highest prediction-target correlation of all Phase-1 runs (0.4785 vs 0.2756 in ZN-E005), a -20.04 cycle RMSE gain over ZN-E005 (425.01 vs 445.05; and -75.21 cycles on >1000-cycle cells), zero extreme negative predictions, the only GELU run that passes all 20-cell ZN-coin domain guardrails vs ZN-E005 (ΔMAPE +0.0110 <= 0.03, ΔAcc@15 -0.0390 <= 0.05), and 0.00% late near-zero gradients in cycle_stem, inter_summary, and head. (2) Crucially, ZN-E010's explicit per-cycle Cycle-1 anchor u_t = [h_t, h_t - h_1] provides the exact trajectory-relative representation needed for Phase-2 what-if fade/trend physics losses (P0/P4b) and tail-balanced losses (stat_tail_balance) to push long-life predictions upward once Phase 1 freezes.
